chains.title: TCF7L2-dependent regulation of POU5F1B
chains.element: The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, but its target gene is not established.
chains.cell_type: HCT116 cells are a candidate context for testing this mechanism.

links.claim: TCF7L2 is expressed and ChIP-bound over the variant in HCT116. QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger binding to ref G in a CIS-BP-mapped LEF1 model; another mapped TCF-family model also detects a change, but there is no TCF7L2-specific model here. This makes TCF7L2 a plausible, not confirmed, allele-sensitive factor. The strong predicted site and HCT116 occupancy favor it over candidates whose changes are weak or not detected, but do not establish TF-specific binding.
The variant lies in enhancer-like pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the evidence does not show which gene this element regulates.

POU5F1B is a candidate target because it is nearby, has a T-associated increase in transverse-colon expression, and has genetic-association support for colorectal cancer. These data do not connect this cCRE to POU5F1B or establish that the eQTL is mediated by TCF7L2.
HCT116 is a relevant test context because TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant and expression of TCF7L2 are reported there; this does not establish the mechanism in primary colorectal tissue.

One possible model is that ref-favored TCF7L2 binding represses POU5F1B, so T increases its expression and could contribute to colorectal cancer susceptibility. The repressive role and causal chain are unproven, and colorectal cancer association records do not resolve the risk-allele direction across studies.

predictions: In an allele-specific TCF7L2 binding assay, ref G should bind more strongly than alt T.
If TCF7L2 represses this element, T should increase POU5F1B expression relative to G; disrupting TCF7L2 binding should diminish that expression difference.
falsified_if: A suitably powered allele-specific assay finds no TCF7L2 binding difference between G and T.
Variant editing produces no reproducible POU5F1B regulatory difference, or TCF7L2 perturbation does not affect that difference.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: Changing G to T will not reproducibly cause a TF-dependent change in local regulatory activity or target-gene expression.
The association may reflect linkage to another causal variant or a mechanism not mediated by TF binding at this base.
falsified_if: Isogenic variant editing reproducibly changes allele-specific TF occupancy and regulatory output, and perturbing the implicated TF removes or materially reduces the effect.

chains.title: SP1-dependent regulation of POU5F1B
chains.element: The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, but its target gene is not established.
chains.cell_type: HCT116 cells are a candidate context for testing this mechanism.

links.claim: SP1 is expressed and ChIP-bound over the variant in HCT116. The SP1-specific QBiC-SELEX model does not detect a clear allelic change; the ref-favoring signal comes from a CIS-BP-mapped SP4 model and is at a weak predicted site. Thus SP1 occupancy is supported, but an SP1-specific allelic binding effect is weakly supported.
The variant lies in enhancer-like pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; no evidence directly assigns this element to POU5F1B.
POU5F1B is a candidate target based on proximity, the T-associated transverse-colon eQTL, and colorectal cancer genetic-association support, but mediation by this cCRE or by SP1 is not demonstrated.
HCT116 is a plausible test context because SP1 occupancy over the variant and SP1 expression are reported there.

If ref-bound SP1 represses POU5F1B at this element, T could increase POU5F1B and affect colorectal cancer susceptibility. Neither SP1 repression nor this causal disease mechanism is established, and the association records do not resolve risk-allele direction.

predictions: A direct SP1-specific assay should find greater binding to ref G than alt T; the current SP1-specific QBiC-SELEX model does not itself provide clear support for this prediction.
If ref-bound SP1 represses POU5F1B, T should increase POU5F1B expression, and SP1 perturbation should reduce the allele-dependent expression difference.
falsified_if: SP1-specific allele assays show no reproducible binding difference and SP1 perturbation has no effect on allele-dependent regulation.
The proposed expression direction is absent in a context where the element is active.

chains.title: SRF-dependent regulation of POU5F1B
chains.element: The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, but its target gene is not established.
chains.cell_type: HCT116 cells are a candidate context for testing this mechanism.

links.claim: SRF is expressed and ChIP-bound over the variant in HCT116. Its own QBiC-SELEX model detects stronger binding to ref G, but the predicted site is weak, so the ChIP peak may reflect another site in the element rather than allele-sensitive binding at this base.
The variant lies in enhancer-like pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the evidence does not establish this element's target gene.
POU5F1B is a candidate target based on proximity, its T-associated transverse-colon eQTL, and colorectal cancer genetic-association support; no evidence links this cCRE to POU5F1B through SRF.
HCT116 is a plausible test context because SRF occupancy over the variant and SRF expression are reported there.

An SRF-dependent change in POU5F1B regulation could affect colorectal cancer susceptibility, but SRF's regulatory direction, the element-to-gene connection, and the causal link to disease are not established. Association records also disagree on risk-allele direction.

predictions: An allele-specific SRF assay should find greater binding to ref G than alt T, although the weak predicted site makes a null result plausible.
If ref-bound SRF activates POU5F1B, T should lower POU5F1B expression; this direction differs from the T-associated increase reported in transverse colon.
falsified_if: A suitably powered SRF-specific assay shows no allele-dependent binding at the variant.
SRF perturbation does not affect any allele-dependent POU5F1B response through this element.

grades_v0.reason: TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant in HCT116 and a ref-favoring QBiC-SELEX change are reported, but the QBiC result uses a CIS-BP-mapped LEF1 model rather than a TCF7L2-specific model. This is indirect support for a TCF7L2-specific allelic effect.
The variant is directly reported inside pELS cCRE EH38E3858447. The claim appropriately does not assign the element to a particular gene.

POU5F1B is nearby, and GTEx reports higher POU5F1B expression with the T allele in transverse colon. These support it as a candidate target, though they do not establish that this cCRE mediates the eQTL.
ENCODE reports TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant in HCT116, directly supporting HCT116 as a candidate test context. The claim appropriately avoids extending this to primary colorectal tissue.

The variant has colorectal cancer associations, the T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B expression in transverse colon, and literature links POU5F1B levels to colon-cancer phenotypes. But the proposed TCF7L2-to-POU5F1B mechanism and its contribution to susceptibility are not demonstrated; CRC risk-allele directions also vary across records.

SP1 occupancy over the variant in HCT116 and a ref-favoring QBiC-SELEX change are reported, but the change comes from a CIS-BP-mapped SP4 model, not an SP1-specific model, and the predicted site is weak. This is indirect support for SP1-specific allelic binding.
The variant is directly reported inside pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, and the claim does not assert a demonstrated target-gene connection.
Proximity and the T-associated increase in POU5F1B expression in transverse colon support POU5F1B as a candidate target, but do not show that this cCRE mediates the eQTL.
ENCODE reports SP1 occupancy over the variant in HCT116, supporting the stated candidate context.

There is variant-level CRC association evidence and indirect support for POU5F1B involvement in colon cancer, but no evidence that SP1 mediates the regulatory effect or that this mechanism causes susceptibility. CRC risk-allele directions vary across records.

grades_final.reason: TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant in HCT116 is reported, but the ref-favoring QBiC-SELEX result comes from a LEF1-mapped model, not a TCF7L2-specific model. Another mapped TCF-family model detects a change in the opposite direction. This supports plausibility, not TCF7L2-specific allele-sensitive binding.
The variant is directly reported within pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the claim appropriately does not assign a target gene.

The evidence supports POU5F1B as a candidate through proximity, a T-associated POU5F1B eQTL in transverse colon, and reported colorectal-cancer association support. It does not establish that this cCRE targets POU5F1B, as the claim acknowledges.
TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant and TCF7L2 expression are reported in HCT116, supporting its use as a candidate test context, not as proof of the mechanism in primary tissue.

The colorectal-cancer association and POU5F1B-related evidence make a contribution plausible, and the proposed direction is consistent with the T-associated expression increase if ref-favored TCF7L2 binding represses the gene. No evidence establishes TCF7L2 repression or the causal variant-to-gene-to-disease chain; the claim appropriately labels these as unproven.

SP1 occupancy over the variant in HCT116 is reported, but the SP1-specific QBiC-SELEX model does not pass the change threshold. The ref-favoring result is from a weak-site SP4-mapped model, so it does not establish an SP1-specific allelic effect.
The variant is directly reported within pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the claim appropriately states that no target-gene assignment is shown.
Proximity, the POU5F1B transverse-colon eQTL, and colorectal-cancer association support POU5F1B as a candidate, while the evidence does not establish cCRE or SP1 mediation.
SP1 occupancy over the variant and SP1 expression are reported in HCT116, supporting its use as a candidate test context.

The variant's colorectal-cancer association and POU5F1B-related evidence are consistent with a possible contribution, but there is no evidence that SP1 represses POU5F1B or mediates the association. The proposed conditional mechanism is appropriately presented as unestablished.

SRF ChIP occupancy over the variant in HCT116 and an above-threshold SRF-model QBiC-SELEX change both support the stated ref-favored binding direction. The weak predicted site limits confidence that the ChIP peak reflects binding at this exact motif, as the claim notes.
The variant is directly reported within pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; the claim appropriately does not assign a target gene.
Proximity, the POU5F1B transverse-colon eQTL, and colorectal-cancer association support POU5F1B as a candidate, but do not establish that the cCRE regulates it through SRF.
SRF occupancy over the variant and SRF expression are reported in HCT116, supporting its use as a candidate test context.

The variant association and POU5F1B-related evidence are consistent with a possible disease contribution, but no evidence establishes SRF's regulatory direction, the element-to-gene link, or causal mediation. The claim appropriately leaves these unresolved.

checks.why: Clarifies whether the variant-level QBiC result supports TCF7L2 specifically or only through the mapped LEF1 model.
Clarifies the SP1 coverage and the relevance of the SP4-mapped prediction to the named TF.
Tests whether disease-association evidence supports POU5F1B as a CRC gene beyond proximity and the cited expression context.

matrix.test: Allele-specific EMSA using G and T probes with TCF7L2-specific validation (for example, supershift or competition controls).

outcomes.outcome: Greater TCF7L2-specific binding to the G probe.
No necessary TCF7L2-specific G-versus-T difference; the proposed factor is SP1.
No reproducible allele-dependent TF binding attributable to this variant.
No necessary TCF7L2-specific G-versus-T difference; the proposed factor is SRF.

matrix.test: Allele-specific SP1 binding assay in HCT116, followed by SP1 perturbation if a difference is detected.

outcomes.outcome: No SP1-specific allelic effect is required; TCF7L2 binding should be the more relevant effect.
Greater SP1 binding to G and an SP1-dependent allele effect on regulatory output.
No reproducible allele-dependent SP1 binding or SP1-dependent regulatory output.
No SP1-specific allelic effect is required; SRF is the proposed factor.

matrix.test: Allele-specific SRF binding assay in HCT116, with SRF perturbation to test regulatory dependence.

outcomes.outcome: No SRF-dependent allele effect is required; TCF7L2 is the proposed factor.
No SRF-dependent allele effect is required; SP1 is the proposed factor.
No reproducible allele-dependent SRF binding or SRF-dependent regulatory output.
Greater SRF binding to G and an SRF-dependent allele effect on regulatory output.

matrix.test: Isogenic G-to-T editing in HCT116 followed by POU5F1B expression measurement with and without TCF7L2 perturbation.

outcomes.outcome: T increases POU5F1B under the proposed repression model, and TCF7L2 perturbation reduces the allele-dependent difference.
Any allele-dependent expression effect should track SP1 perturbation rather than TCF7L2 perturbation.
No reproducible allele-dependent POU5F1B expression effect or TF-dependent interaction.
Any allele-dependent expression effect should track SRF perturbation rather than TCF7L2 perturbation.

next_experiment: Run the low-cost TCF7L2-specific allele-probe EMSA with G and T sequences and supershift or competition controls. Greater TCF7L2-specific binding to G would support H1 over the null; no difference would weaken its central binding premise. This tests binding directly but would not by itself establish regulation of POU5F1B or a disease effect.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401060:G>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 64 occupied (19 with a strong site), 5 of 133 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 6 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 497 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 6 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
